citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
citations.narrative:
Two adult beagles, microchip numbers 933000321303321 and 933000321204465 were identified as having a moderate
amount of thick, hard, brown, grey material (tartar) on the molars and premolars. The medical records, including the last
annual exam, do not note this finding or any method of prevention or treatment.
Poor dental health can make it difficult to chew food, cause discomfort, and may lead to health issues. The facility shall
ensure the use of appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose and treat diseases, such as dental disease, to
ensure the health and well-being of the dogs. A system should be in place to identify dental issues and provide regular
dental care.
Correct by August 15, 2026.

Medical records were not available at the time of inspection for three adult beagles. Two beagles, microchip numbers
933000321302784 and 933000321274283, were euthanized in June 2025 and one beagle, microchip
#933000321182264, was euthanized in May 2025.
Medical records for dogs shall be kept and maintained by the research facility for the duration of the research activity and
for an additional 3 years after the dog is euthanized or disposed of, and for any period in excess of 3 years as necessary
to comply with any applicable Federal, State, or local law.
Correct from this day forward.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
